places.title: Vinci
places.text: Born near Vinci and raised in the household of his grandfather Antonio and his uncle Francesco. The childhood residence is documented, the move to Florence is dated by estimate.
places.basis: Family note of Antonio da Vinci; 1457 Florentine tax return.

places.title: Florence, apprentice
places.text: Apprenticeship in the workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio. No apprenticeship contract survives, so both ends of this bar are scholarly estimates.
places.basis: Inferred from later records and from workshop practice.

places.title: Florence, master
places.text: Listed in the painters' company in 1472, recorded in Verrocchio's household in 1476, then commissioned independently in 1478 and 1481.
places.basis: Company of San Luca register; Ufficiali di Notte record, 1476; commission records, 1478 and 1481.

places.title: Milan
places.text: Employed at the court of Ludovico Sforza. Presence in Milan is documented from the 1483 Virgin of the Rocks contract. The date of arrival is not recorded.
places.basis: Contract of 25 April 1483; court and cathedral records.

places.title: Mantua, Venice
places.text: After the French conquest of Milan he travelled to Mantua, where he drew Isabella d'Este, and was in Venice by mid March 1500.
places.basis: Letter of Lorenzo Gusnasco to Isabella d'Este, 13 March 1500.

places.title: Florence
places.text: Back in Florence by spring 1500, working at the Servite house of Santissima Annunziata. Fra Pietro da Novellara reports on his work in April 1501.
places.basis: Novellara letter of 3 April 1501; financial records.

places.title: Romagna
places.place: Imola, Cesena, Urbino and the Romagna
places.text: Military architect and engineer in the service of Cesare Borgia. Travel through Urbino, Pesaro, Rimini, Cesena and Imola.
places.basis: Passport dated 18 August 1502; maps and notes in his own hand.

places.title: Florence
places.text: Working on the Battle of Anghiari for the Council Hall and, in the same years, on the Mona Lisa and on Arno projects.
places.basis: Commission of 4 May 1504; payment records; his own notes.

places.title: Milan
places.place: Milan, with interludes in Florence and Pavia
places.text: Called to Milan by Charles d'Amboise in 1506. Returned to Florence for the inheritance dispute in 1507 and 1508, and lived in the Melzi household at Vaprio d'Adda in part of 1513.
places.basis: Florentine leave of absence, 1506; his notes dated Milan; inheritance suit records.

places.title: Rome
places.text: Left Milan for Rome on 24 September 1513 and lived in the Belvedere at the Vatican under Giuliano de' Medici.
places.basis: His own note on the departure; Vatican payment lists.

places.title: Cloux, Amboise
places.text: Lived at the manor of Cloux near the royal château at Amboise. His presence is documented in October 1517 and at the will of April 1519.
places.basis: Travel diary of Antonio de Beatis, 10 October 1517; will of 23 April 1519.

works.title: Arno valley landscape
works.text: Pen drawing of a river valley with a dated inscription. It is the earliest securely dated sheet by Leonardo.

works.title: Baptism of Christ (Verrocchio)
works.text: Workshop painting by Verrocchio. Leonardo's hand is generally recognised in the left angel and parts of the landscape. The allocation of passages is a scholarly judgement.
works.basis: Style and technique; attribution of passages.

works.title: Annunciation
works.text: Early panel now in the Uffizi, dated by style. Its attribution to Leonardo is widely accepted.

works.title: Ginevra de' Benci
works.text: Portrait of a young Florentine woman with a juniper motif on the reverse. The dating rests on style and on the identification of the sitter.
works.basis: Stylistic dating; heraldry and emblem on the reverse.

works.title: Hanged man, Baroncelli
works.text: Study of the hanged conspirator Bernardo di Bandino Baroncelli with notes on his clothing, drawn on the day of the execution.

works.title: Madonna of the Carnation
works.text: Early Madonna panel, dated by style. Some scholars debate the share of workshop assistance.

works.title: Benois Madonna
works.text: Madonna with a flower held out to the child. Dated by style to the last Florentine years.

works.title: Adoration of the Magi
works.text: Commissioned in March 1481 by the monks of San Donato a Scopeto and left unfinished when Leonardo moved to Milan. The date of the commission is documented, the state of the underdrawing is a matter for study.

works.title: St Jerome
works.text: Unfinished panel in monochrome underpainting. Its dating is disputed between the late Florentine and early Milanese years.

works.title: Sforza horse
works.text: Project for a monumental bronze equestrian statue of Francesco Sforza. A full scale clay model was shown in November 1493 and damaged in 1499. The bronze was never cast.
works.basis: Court correspondence; Leonardo's notes and drawings.

works.title: Virgin of the Rocks (Louvre)
works.text: The contract with the Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception is dated 25 April 1483. The painting's date within the following years is an estimate. A second version in London was completed later after a legal dispute.

works.title: Portrait of a Musician
works.text: Unfinished male portrait. The face is generally accepted as Leonardo's, while the extent of his participation and the identity of the sitter are debated.

works.title: Milan Cathedral crossing model
works.text: Leonardo is paid for a model for the crossing tower of Milan Cathedral and consults on the design.

works.title: Paris Manuscript B
works.text: Small notebook with studies of flying machines, fortifications and ideal city design. Now in the Institut de France.

works.title: Codex Trivulzianus
works.text: Notebook with long word lists and architectural sketches, now in Milan.

works.title: Skull studies
works.text: Sheets of a skull in section and in several views. A dated inscription marks the drawings.

works.title: Lady with an Ermine
works.text: Portrait of a woman from the Sforza court. The identification as Cecilia Gallerani is an interpretation that rests on the ermine emblem and a contemporary sonnet.
works.basis: Stylistic dating; identification of sitter is interpretive.

works.title: Vitruvian Man
works.text: Pen drawing on proportions after Vitruvius. Dated to about 1490 on stylistic and notebook grounds.

works.title: Madrid Codices I and II
works.text: Two notebooks on mechanics and geometry, rediscovered in Madrid in 1966. The first belongs to the Milan years, the second to the years in Florence.

works.title: Polyhedra for Pacioli
works.text: Illustrations of regular and semi regular solids for Luca Pacioli's De divina proportione. Manuscript copies are dated 1498, and the printed book appeared in 1509.

works.title: Last Supper
works.text: Wall painting in the refectory. Ducal correspondence of 1497 presses for completion, but the beginning and end of the work are estimates. Its technical condition is a separate question from its dating.
works.basis: Ducal correspondence, 1497; stylistic and technical study.

works.title: Sala delle Asse
works.text: Decoration of the ceiling of a hall in the Sforza castle with interlaced trees. The work is dated by court correspondence to 1498.

works.title: Portrait of Isabella d'Este
works.text: Profile drawing in chalk, made at Mantua. Isabella pressed for a painted version for several years.
works.basis: Correspondence of Isabella d'Este; stylistic dating.

works.title: Burlington House Cartoon
works.text: Large charcoal cartoon of the Virgin, Child, St Anne and St John. The date is disputed between the late Milan years and 1506 to 1508.

works.title: Salvator Mundi
works.text: Half length Christ with a crystal orb. Attribution to Leonardo is accepted by some scholars and disputed by others.

works.title: Servite St Anne cartoon (lost)
works.text: Cartoon of the Virgin and St Anne known from descriptions, among them the Novellara letter. The relation to the later compositions is an interpretation.

works.title: Madonna of the Yarnwinder
works.text: The Novellara letter describes a small Madonna with a yarnwinder commissioned for Florimond Robertet. Surviving versions are not securely tied to that description.

works.title: Map of Imola
works.text: Town plan drawn with surveying methods during his service with Cesare Borgia.

works.title: Mona Lisa
works.text: Portrait of a woman widely identified as Lisa del Giocondo. The Vespucci note of October 1503 is the main contemporary evidence. The painting was probably worked on over many years.
works.basis: Vespucci note, 1503; stylistic and technical study.

works.title: Battle of Anghiari
works.text: Wall painting for the Council Hall with a cartoon completed in 1504 and painting begun in 1505. The experiment in oil technique failed and the work was abandoned. It is known from copies.
works.basis: Contract of 4 May 1504; his own note of 6 June 1505.

works.title: Codex on the Flight of Birds
works.text: Notebook on bird flight and flying machines, with the note on a planned flight from Monte Ceceri.

works.title: Leda and the Swan (lost)
works.text: Known only through copies and drawings. The date of the lost original is estimated from the studies.

works.title: Codex Leicester
works.text: Notebook on water, the Earth and the Moon, with fossil observations.

works.title: Anatomical studies, Florence
works.text: Studies after the dissection of an old man at the hospital, according to his own notes on the sheets at Windsor.

works.title: Trivulzio monument
works.text: Design and costing for an equestrian funerary monument for Marshal Gian Giacomo Trivulzio. It was not built.

works.title: Virgin and Child with St Anne
works.text: Panel on which he worked over many years. Its date is an estimate that spans the later part of his career.

works.title: Anatomical studies, Milan and Pavia
works.text: Windsor sheets on the heart, vessels and the body in motion. The link with Marcantonio della Torre rests on Vasari.

works.title: St John the Baptist
works.text: Half length figure pointing upward. Dated to the last years by style.

works.title: Deluge drawings
works.text: Late series of black chalk drawings of storms and floods.

works.title: Romorantin residence and canal
works.text: Project for a royal residence and canal system for Francis I. The surviving sheets are plans and notes, not a built work.

works.title: Codex Atlanticus (content)
works.text: A late sixteenth century assembly of sheets by Pompeo Leoni. The sheets themselves date from the whole of Leonardo's active life.

people.title: Ser Piero da Vinci
people.text: Notary and Leonardo's father. Leonardo, born out of wedlock, did not share in his estate.
people.basis: Family notes; tax returns; Leonardo's note of 1504.

people.title: Francesco da Vinci
people.text: Uncle of Leonardo. His will named Leonardo, and the half brothers contested it after his death.

people.title: Andrea del Verrocchio
people.text: Painter, sculptor and goldsmith whose workshop trained Leonardo. A 1476 record places Leonardo in his household. The start of the relationship is estimated.

people.title: Perugino and Lorenzo di Credi
people.text: Contemporaries in Verrocchio's circle. The bar shows shared workshop years, not a recorded friendship. Contact with Leonardo is inferred from workshop context.

people.title: Lorenzo de' Medici
people.text: Later biographers place Leonardo in his circle and say he sent him to Milan with a silver lyre. Contemporary evidence is thin.

people.title: Ludovico Sforza
people.text: Duke of Milan and Leonardo's principal patron during the Milan years.

people.title: Ambrogio and Evangelista de Predis
people.text: Partners in the 1483 Virgin of the Rocks contract. A long dispute over payment was settled in the later years.

people.title: Donato Bramante
people.text: Architect at the Sforza court. The bar shows the years both were in Milan, not a recorded friendship. Shared interest in central plan churches is traced in Leonardo's sketches. The contact is inferred from overlap in time and subject.
people.basis: Inference from co presence in Milan.

people.title: Boltraffio and Marco d'Oggiono
people.text: Milanese painters working in the manner of Leonardo. Their status as pupils or associates is debated.

people.title: Salai (Gian Giacomo Caprotti)
people.text: Joined the household aged ten and remained in his circle for decades. The 1519 will leaves him half of the Milan vineyard.

people.title: Cecilia Gallerani
people.text: Identified as the sitter of the Lady with an Ermine. The identification rests on the ermine emblem and a sonnet by Bellincioni.

people.title: Luca Pacioli
people.text: Franciscan mathematician at the Sforza court. Leonardo drew the solids for his De divina proportione. Their travel together after 1499 is an inference.
people.basis: Pacioli's dedications; sources on the departure from Milan.

people.title: Isabella d'Este
people.text: Marchioness of Mantua. She sat for a drawing in 1499 and sought a painting through agents for years.

people.title: Fra Pietro da Novellara
people.text: Carmelite vicar who reported on Leonardo's work to Isabella d'Este.

people.title: Cesare Borgia
people.text: Employed Leonardo as military architect and engineer.

people.title: Niccolò Machiavelli
people.text: Florentine secretary, present at the Borgia court in autumn 1502 and involved in the Arno project. The documents establish overlap, while any personal friendship is an interpretation.

people.title: Pier Soderini
people.text: Head of the Florentine government during the Anghiari commission and the leave of 1506.

people.title: Lisa Gherardini and Francesco del Giocondo
people.text: The Vespucci note links Lisa del Giocondo with a portrait by Leonardo. That the Louvre panel is that portrait rests on later sources and scholarly argument.

people.title: Michelangelo Buonarroti
people.text: Rival commission in the Council Hall (Battle of Cascina). Both artists were in Florence at the same time, which is documented. The bar shows this overlap, not a recorded friendship. Direct exchange between them is mostly reported by later writers.

people.title: Raphael
people.text: In Florence from 1504 until he left for Rome in 1508. The bar shows the years both were in the city, not a recorded friendship. Raphael's drawings after Leonardo's compositions indicate study, which is an inference.
people.basis: Raphael's residence in Florence; drawings and compositional parallels.

people.title: Charles d'Amboise
people.text: French governor of Milan. Asked Florence for Leonardo in 1506 and employed him as painter and engineer.

people.title: Francesco Melzi
people.text: Young Milanese nobleman who became Leonardo's closest assistant and heir. He kept the notebooks after 1519. The start of the relationship is estimated.

people.title: Gian Giacomo Trivulzio
people.text: Marshal in French service for whom Leonardo planned a funerary monument.

people.title: Marcantonio della Torre
people.text: Vasari reports a collaboration on anatomy. No contemporary document confirms it.

people.title: Giuliano de' Medici
people.text: Brother of Pope Leo X. Provided Belvedere quarters and payments.

people.title: Francis I
people.text: King of France who brought Leonardo to the Loire and housed him at Cloux.

people.title: Antonio de Beatis
people.text: Secretary of Cardinal Luigi d'Aragona. His diary records a visit to Leonardo.

people.title: Guillaume Boreau
people.text: Royal notary who drew up the will.

events.title: Birth
events.text: Born on a Saturday, as recorded by his grandfather Antonio in a family note. Baptised at Vinci.
events.basis: Family note of Antonio da Vinci.

events.title: Tax return of 1457
events.text: Antonio da Vinci's tax return lists Leonardo, aged five, as the illegitimate son of Ser Piero and a woman named Caterina.

events.title: Enters Verrocchio's workshop
events.text: The usual estimate places his entry at about age fourteen. No contract survives.
events.basis: Estimate from later biographies and the 1472 guild entry.

events.title: Painters' company of San Luca
events.text: Enrolled as a painter in the Florentine company of San Luca.

events.title: Anonymous denunciation
events.text: An anonymous accusation naming Leonardo and others was lodged with the Ufficiali di Notte. The case was dismissed on 7 June 1476. The record also places him in Verrocchio's household.
events.basis: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Ufficiali di Notte.

events.title: Chapel of San Bernardo commission
events.text: First independent public commission: an altarpiece for the chapel of San Bernardo. It was never delivered and was reassigned in 1481.

events.title: Letter to Ludovico Sforza
events.text: A draft letter offering skills in military engineering and noting his ability as painter and sculptor. Whether it was sent, and exactly when, is not known.
events.basis: Codex Atlanticus; dating is an editorial estimate.

events.title: Salai enters the household
events.text: Gian Giacomo Caprotti, called Salai, aged ten, joins the household. Leonardo's note records the cost of his clothes and a list of his thefts.

events.title: Vineyard granted
events.text: Ludovico Sforza grants Leonardo a vineyard outside the Porta Vercellina. Leonardo later bequeaths it in his will.

events.title: Leaves Milan
events.text: Departs for Mantua and Venice, probably in company with Luca Pacioli. Records show 600 florins placed at Santa Maria Nuova in Florence on 14 December 1499.
events.basis: Hospital account of Santa Maria Nuova; the companionship with Pacioli is an inference.

events.title: In Venice
events.text: A letter to Isabella d'Este reports that Leonardo is in Venice.

events.title: Novellara letter
events.text: The Carmelite Fra Pietro da Novellara tells Isabella d'Este that Leonardo is working on a small Madonna with a yarnwinder and has made little progress with the St Anne cartoon.
events.basis: Letter of Fra Pietro da Novellara, 3 April 1501.

events.title: Passport from Cesare Borgia
events.text: Cesare Borgia names Leonardo architect and general engineer with free passage through his territories.

events.title: Arno diversion project
events.text: Leonardo advises the Florentine government on diverting the Arno to cut off Pisa. Niccolò Machiavelli was involved on the government side. The works failed in 1504.

events.title: Vespucci marginal note
events.text: Agostino Vespucci notes in a printed book that Leonardo is painting a portrait of Lisa del Giocondo. This note is the principal contemporary link to the Mona Lisa.
events.basis: Marginal note in a volume of Cicero, Heidelberg University Library.

events.title: David placement committee
events.text: Leonardo is among the artists consulted on the placement of Michelangelo's David.

events.title: Death of Ser Piero
events.text: Leonardo records the death of his father in his own hand. As an illegitimate son he did not share in the estate.

events.title: Begins to paint at the Palazzo
events.text: His note records the day he began to paint the Battle of Anghiari on the wall of the Council Hall.

events.title: Leave to Milan
events.text: Charles d'Amboise asks Florence for Leonardo. The republic grants a leave of limited length that is later extended.

events.title: Inheritance dispute
events.text: After the death of his uncle Francesco, Leonardo's half brothers contest the will. Leonardo returns to Florence for the suit.

events.title: Death of Charles d'Amboise
events.text: The French governor of Milan dies, ending a patron relationship begun in 1506.

events.title: Departs for Rome
events.text: Leonardo notes his departure from Milan for Rome with Melzi, Salai and two assistants.

events.title: Mechanical lion at Lyon
events.text: Later writers credit Leonardo with a mechanical lion for the entry of Francis I into Lyon. The attribution rests on tradition.

events.title: Death of Giuliano de' Medici
events.text: The patron who housed Leonardo in the Belvedere dies, which opens the way to the French invitation.

events.title: Moves to France
events.text: Leonardo crosses the Alps with Melzi at the invitation of Francis I. The exact date is not recorded.
events.basis: Later documents; the arrival is inferred from 1517.

events.title: Beatis visit
events.text: Antonio de Beatis visits and describes three paintings in the house and Leonardo's paralysed right hand.
events.basis: Travel diary of Antonio de Beatis.

events.title: Amboise festivities
events.text: Later writers credit Leonardo with stage design and machinery for royal festivities at Amboise. The attribution rests on tradition.

events.title: Will
events.text: Leonardo's will names Francesco Melzi heir to books and instruments and divides the Milan vineyard between Salai and a servant.
events.basis: Notarial act drawn up at Amboise.

events.title: Death
events.text: Leonardo dies. Melzi announces the death in a letter to the half brothers on 1 June 1519.

popes.title: Nicholas V
popes.text: Pope at the time of Leonardo's birth. Founded the Vatican Library and began the rebuilding of Rome. Succeeded by Callixtus III.

popes.title: Callixtus III
popes.text: Alfons de Borja, the first Borgia pope and uncle of the future Alexander VI. Elected after Nicholas V and followed by Pius II.

popes.title: Pius II
popes.text: Enea Silvio Piccolomini, a humanist who tried to organise a crusade after the fall of Constantinople. Died at Ancona and was succeeded by Paul II.

popes.title: Paul II
popes.text: Pietro Barbo. His reign covers the years of Leonardo's apprenticeship in Florence. Succeeded by Sixtus IV.

popes.title: Sixtus IV
popes.text: Francesco della Rovere. Excommunicated Lorenzo de' Medici after the Pazzi conspiracy of 1478 and placed Florence under interdict, which led to war. Built the Sistine Chapel. His reign spans Leonardo's independent years in Florence and the move to Milan.

popes.title: Innocent VIII
popes.text: Giovanni Battista Cybo, allied with Lorenzo de' Medici by marriage. Created Lorenzo's son Giovanni, the later Leo X, a cardinal in 1489.

popes.title: Alexander VI
popes.text: Rodrigo Borgia, father of Cesare Borgia, in whose service Leonardo worked in 1502 and 1503. His death in August 1503 ended Cesare's power.

popes.title: Pius III
popes.text: Francesco Todeschini Piccolomini. Reigned for about a month between Alexander VI and Julius II.

popes.title: Julius II
popes.text: Giuliano della Rovere, an enemy of the Borgias. Commissioned Michelangelo's Sistine ceiling and Raphael's rooms in the Vatican. Leonardo was in Florence and Milan throughout his reign.

popes.title: Leo X
popes.text: Giovanni de' Medici, son of Lorenzo and brother of Giuliano de' Medici, Leonardo's patron in Rome. The Belvedere years fall in his reign, which ran beyond the end of the chart.

history.title: Fall of Constantinople
history.text: Ottoman forces under Mehmed II take the Byzantine capital. Greek scholars and manuscripts move west in the following decades.

history.title: Peace of Lodi
history.text: Milan and Venice end their war. The settlement underlies the balance among the Italian states for the next four decades.

history.title: Gutenberg Bible
history.text: First major book printed from movable type in Europe. The date is an estimate.

history.title: Death of Francesco Sforza
history.text: The Duke of Milan dies and is succeeded by his son Galeazzo Maria Sforza.

history.title: Lorenzo takes power in Florence
history.text: After the death of his father Piero, Lorenzo de' Medici, aged twenty, becomes the leading figure of the Florentine state.

history.title: Galeazzo Maria Sforza killed
history.text: The duke is assassinated in the church of Santo Stefano. His widow rules for his young son, and the way opens for his brother Ludovico.

history.title: Pazzi conspiracy
history.text: Giuliano de' Medici is murdered at Mass in the cathedral and Lorenzo is wounded but escapes. Many conspirators are hanged. Bernardo di Bandino Baroncelli, who fled, is brought back and hanged in December 1479, the event Leonardo drew.
history.basis: Standard chronologies; Leonardo's dated drawing of 29 December 1479.

history.title: War after the Pazzi plot
history.text: Pope Sixtus IV and Naples fight Florence. Lorenzo travels to Naples in December 1479 and secures peace in March 1480.

history.title: Ottomans take Otranto
history.text: Ottoman forces capture the Italian port. The shock helps to end the Pazzi war.

history.title: Ludovico takes control in Milan
history.text: Ludovico Sforza ends the regency of Cicco Simonetta and becomes the effective ruler of Milan for his nephew Gian Galeazzo.

history.title: Sistine Chapel wall frescoes
history.text: Florentine painters including Botticelli, Perugino, Ghirlandaio and Cosimo Rosselli are called to Rome by Sixtus IV. Leonardo is not among them.

history.title: Fall of Granada
history.text: The last Muslim kingdom in Iberia falls to Castile and Aragon.

history.title: Death of Lorenzo de' Medici
history.text: Lorenzo dies and is succeeded by his son Piero.

history.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
history.text: Christopher Columbus, a Genoese in Spanish service, lands in the Caribbean.

history.title: Charles VIII invades Italy
history.text: Charles VIII of France crosses the Alps, enters Florence and Naples, and then retreats. Italy becomes a battlefield of the French and Spanish crowns for decades.

history.title: Ludovico becomes Duke of Milan
history.text: Gian Galeazzo Sforza dies and Ludovico takes the ducal title.

history.title: Medici expelled from Florence
history.text: Piero de' Medici flees as the French approach. A republic influenced by Savonarola follows.

history.title: Aldine Press, Venice
history.text: Aldus Manutius begins to publish Greek and Latin classics in Venice. The starting year is approximate.

history.title: Savonarola executed
history.text: Girolamo Savonarola is hanged and burned in the Piazza della Signoria.

history.title: French take Milan
history.text: The army of Louis XII conquers the duchy and Ludovico Sforza flees. Later tradition says French troops damaged the clay model of the Sforza horse.
history.basis: Standard chronologies; the model's fate rests on later sources.

history.title: Cesare Borgia in the Romagna
history.text: Cesare Borgia conquers the cities of the Romagna with papal and French backing. His power collapses after the death of Alexander VI.

history.title: Sistine Chapel ceiling
history.text: Michelangelo paints the ceiling for Julius II. It is unveiled on 1 November 1512.

history.title: League of Cambrai
history.text: The pope, France, Spain and the Empire ally against Venice. The war opens with the battle of Agnadello on 14 May 1509.

history.title: French driven from Milan
history.text: The Holy League expels the French and Massimiliano Sforza is restored in December.

history.title: Medici return to Florence
history.text: The republic falls after the sack of Prato and the Medici come back.

history.title: Francis I becomes king
history.text: Francis I succeeds Louis XII.

history.title: Battle of Marignano
history.text: Francis I defeats the Swiss and takes Milan. He meets Leo X at Bologna in December.

history.title: Ninety five Theses
history.text: Martin Luther publishes his theses against indulgences, the usual starting point of the Reformation.
